verdict.why: X is the better implementation base because its failure path honors both “one request each” and “every token call.” X Design §§4–5 and T9–T17 specify one POST, no retry, and a task-attributed row even on timeout, with unknown cost rather than an assumed zero. Y R7 explicitly tests that a validator is called twice and booked once; C4 and Q8 extend that retry to research validation. A missing usage response does not establish that the provider did no billable work. Both preserve panel spend on judge-only reruns, but X also checks the cost rule against BYOK and non-BYOK provider fixtures (Rollout §2). X routes new decisions back to the thinker regardless of size and checks for stale meanings revisions (Design §§1–3); Y exempts S and refuses a thinker plan call for M even when planning decides something (D2, C4). Y is stronger on council configuration: C8 enforces the named five and derives the judge directly from the thinker role. Its `unknown` estate state is also safer than X's local-only fallback. Those are worth adopting without Y's retry and accounting rules.
risks: X can still ship the superseded workflow: no role map restores session authorship, `--from-file` permits subscription meanings, and an existing six-seat config remains valid (Design §§2–4). Rollout §4 should verify the owner's actual model/route assignments and exact roster before enabling the release.

X T22 skips the judge when the panel alone exceeds its cap. That withholds the required Fable verdict after the validators have already been paid. Y C8 separates the two outcomes correctly: obtain the verdict when quorum exists, then fail the panel budget check.

Neither option completes owner-surface delivery: X Rollout §7 and Y Rollout §4 create Observatory board rows, not a verified day/month view. X Design §6 can also report `ok` from this host alone or use a cache of any age; neither establishes current estate headroom.

X's append-only accounting has no working correction contract: C6 `record` appends a row, but `check` still rejects the original successful null-cost row. Y has a different cost risk: D15 infers BYOK from relative cost fields, which its own Risks section says can double-count ordinary calls.

X's three-spec canary is feasible but a weak regression gate: deterioration triggers a question whose default is to keep the split (Rollout §6). Y's blind replay is a better direct comparison in principle, but R15 requires two finished M specs and Q23 identifies none in the base repository, leaving the acceptance inputs unresolved.
